title: FUSE: An Evaluating Framework for Dangerous Capabilities of LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2609.02168v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Fragmented safety evaluation undermines the governance of dangerous AI capabilities. We present a modular framework that evaluates each model through three orthogonal pipelines---Knowledge ($K$), Defense ($D$), and Harm ($H$)---under a unified protocol, aggregating results into a standardized dangerous-capability profile $\phi$. Pluggable modules supply scenario seeds, knowledge banks, hazard queries, and judge rubrics, while the core evaluation engine remains unchanged across domains; the CB evaluation is complemented by a cyber pilot demonstrating protocol transfer.   Instantiating the framework with a chemical-biological (CB) module, we evaluate 12 commercial LLMs from four families. Our first contribution is a horizontal comparison of dangerous capability across models and model families: the three dimensions expose sharply divergent profiles---models with comparable knowledge differ in refusal resilience, and strong defenders do not

translated_title: FUSE：一个大语言模型危险能力评估框架
translated_abstract: 碎片化的安全评估削弱了对AI危险能力的治理。我们提出了一个模块化框架，在统一协议下通过三个正交流水线——知识（K）、防御（D）和危害（H）——对每个模型进行评估，并将结果汇总为标准化的危险能力画像 φ。可插拔模块提供场景种子、知识库、危害查询和评判标准，而核心评估引擎在各个领域保持不变；化学生物（CB）评估还辅以一个网络安全试点，以展示协议的可迁移性。我们通过化学生物（CB）模块实例化该框架，评估了来自四个系列的12个商用大语言模型。我们的首要贡献是对各模型及模型系列之间危险能力的横向比较：三个维度揭示了截然不同的能力画像——知识水平相当的模型在抗拒绝能力上存在差异，而防御能力强的模型并不（具备相应特征）。
tldr: 本文提出FUSE框架，在统一协议下通过知识、防御、危害三个正交流水线评估大语言模型的危险能力，并利用化学生物模块对四个系列的12个商用LLM进行横向比较，揭示了各模型间差异显著的危险能力画像。
en_tdlr: FUSE is a modular framework that evaluates LLM dangerous capabilities through three orthogonal pipelines—Knowledge, Defense, and Harm—under a unified protocol, and its chemical-biological instantiation reveals sharply divergent risk profiles across 12 commercial LLMs from four families.
